name: Beplus Link Status Scanner
author: Beplus

sections.description:
Beplus Link Status Scanner scans all your published content for broken links, redirects, and unreachable URLs. It runs in the background using WordPress Cron so your site performance is never impacted.

Key Features

  • Automatic background scanning — Uses WP-Cron to scan posts and check links on a schedule you control.
  • Multi-source scanning — Detects broken links in post content (<a href>), broken images (<img src>), Gutenberg block attributes (embed, button, image, file blocks), ACF custom fields, navigation menus, and widget areas.
  • Link type badges — Every link is tagged by type (Anchor, Image, Block, ACF, Menu, Widget) so you know exactly where a broken URL came from.
  • Broken link report — A clean admin table listing every broken link: URL, type, HTTP status code, the source it was found in, the redirect target, and when it was last checked.
  • Fewer false alarms — A single timeout or server error isn’t reported as broken; the link is re-checked within a day and only flagged as broken if it fails again. Sites that block automated checks (403, 429, LinkedIn’s 999) are shown as “Warning” for you to confirm instead of “Broken”.
  • Only what needs fixing — One list with broken links first, then warnings, then redirects; working links are tracked quietly in the background and never clutter the list. Filter by link type (Anchor, Image, Block, ACF, Menu, Widget) and search by URL.
  • Not broken — Checked a flagged link by hand and it works? Mark it as “Not broken” and it leaves the report. It stays monitored and is reported again only if it starts failing in a different way.
  • Unlink — Remove a broken link from your post while keeping its text, straight from the report (one link or many at once). Button blocks keep their button, and a revision is saved so the change can be undone.
  • Bulk actions — Re-check, mark as not broken, or unlink multiple links at once.
  • Inline link replace — Swap any broken URL directly from the admin table without editing the post or menu manually.
  • Export CSV — Export your link data to a CSV file, filtered by status and link type, from the Export tab.
  • One-click scan — “Scan for broken links” finds every link in your content and checks it in one go, with a live two-step progress bar. The report shows when the last scan ran and how many links are still waiting.
  • Email notifications — Get a digest email listing only newly broken links after each cron check run, grouped by the post, menu or widget they were found in.
  • Configurable settings — Set check frequency (daily/weekly/monthly), request timeout, links per cron run, and excluded URL patterns.
  • Dashboard widget — Broken, warning and redirect counts at a glance on your WordPress dashboard.
  • Always in sync — Posts are re-scanned when saved, links removed from your content disappear from the report, and links from trashed, unpublished or deleted posts and menus are cleaned up automatically.

How It Works

  1. When a post is published or updated, Link Status Scanner extracts all URLs from the content — anchors, images, Gutenberg block attributes, and ACF fields — and stores them in the database.
  2. A daily cron job re-scans all published content, then navigation menus and widget areas. Each run works through as many posts as it can in about 20 seconds, so even large sites are covered quickly.
  3. A second cron job checks each stored URL with an HTTP HEAD request (retrying with GET when a server rejects HEAD) and records the response code.
  4. Links that return 404/410 or other client errors are flagged as broken. Timeouts and server errors are flagged as broken only after failing twice in a row; responses that usually mean “automated requests blocked” are flagged as warnings.
  5. If email notifications are enabled, you receive a digest email listing newly broken links after each check run.

Privacy

Beplus Link Status Scanner sends HTTP requests to external URLs in order to check their status. No personal data is collected or shared.

About BePlus

This plugin is developed and maintained by BePlus, a WordPress and Shopify development studio with 10+ years of experience building themes and plugins for nonprofits and eCommerce brands.

Learn more at beplusthemes.com.

External services

This plugin connects to external URLs in order to perform its core function of checking link status.

When you run a scan (manually or via the scheduled WP-Cron check), Beplus Link Status Scanner sends an HTTP HEAD request (falling back to a GET request, limited to the first 256 KB of the response, when HEAD fails or is rejected) to every URL it finds linked from your own posts, pages, menus, and widgets. These destination URLs are determined entirely by your own site’s content — they are not a fixed third-party service chosen by the plugin — and requests are sent only to check whether each URL is reachable and to record its HTTP response status code.

No personal or user data is included in these requests: only the target URL and a generic User-Agent header identifying the plugin and WordPress version are sent.

Because checking the status of links is the plugin’s entire purpose, this outbound request behavior cannot be disabled independently — it can only be stopped by deactivating the plugin.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the beplus-link-status-scanner folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings > Link Status Scanner to view the broken links report.
  4. Click Scan for broken links to find and check all links right away. After that, links are checked automatically on the schedule you choose.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin slow down my site?

No. All scanning and HTTP checking happens through WP-Cron, which runs in the background. The only admin-side actions are when you manually trigger a scan or re-check.

What types of links are scanned?

The plugin scans <a href> anchors, <img src> images, Gutenberg block attributes (embed URL, button URL, image link, file link), ACF custom fields (URL, link, image, and file field types), navigation menus, and classic/block widget areas. mailto:, tel:, javascript:, and anchor-only # links are automatically skipped.

Can I exclude certain domains or URLs?

Yes. Go to the Settings tab and add URL patterns (one per line) to the Excluded URL Patterns field. Any link containing that pattern will be skipped.

Why does WP-Cron not run on schedule?

WP-Cron triggers on page loads. On low-traffic sites it may not run on time. For reliable scheduling, disable WP-Cron and add a real system cron job:
*/5 * * * * curl -s https://yoursite.com/wp-cron.php?doing_wp_cron > /dev/null 2>&1

What does “Warning” status mean?

Either the site refused the automated check (for example 401, 403, 429 or LinkedIn’s 999 — these links usually work fine in a browser), or the request failed temporarily (timeout, connection error, 5xx). Temporary failures are re-checked within a day and become “Broken” only if they fail again. Open warning links in your browser to confirm, and click “Not broken” for ones that work.

What happens when I click “Not broken”?

The link leaves the report but is still checked on schedule. If it keeps failing the same way (for example LinkedIn’s 999) it stays hidden; if it starts failing differently (for example a 404) it is reported again.

What does “Redirect” status mean?

A redirect (301, 302, 303, 307, 308) means the URL has moved. The link still works but you may want to update it to the final destination for SEO — the redirect target is shown under the status in the report.

Does the plugin work with ACF?

Yes. If Advanced Custom Fields is active, the scanner reads URL, link, image, and file field types. ACF is not required — the scanner simply skips ACF fields when ACF is not installed.

Can I export the results?

Yes. The Export tab lets you download a CSV file of all tracked links. You can filter by status (Broken, Redirect, OK, etc.) and by link type (Anchor, Image, Block, ACF, Menu, Widget) before exporting.
sections.changelog:
1.3.0

  • New: “Warning” status — sites that block automated checks (401, 403, 405, 406, 429, LinkedIn’s 999) are no longer reported as broken, and a single timeout or server error is re-checked within a day and only reported as broken if it fails again.
  • New: When a server rejects the HEAD request (400, 403, 404, 405, 406, 429, 999 or 5xx), the link is retried with a GET request before deciding its status.
  • New: Filter the report by link type (Anchor, Image, Block, ACF, Menu, Widget). Type and search filters now carry over to pagination and sorting.
  • New: “Unlink” action (per row and in bulk) removes a broken link from the post but keeps the link text. Button blocks keep the button without a link; links stored in block settings (such as File blocks) are left for the block editor so the block stays valid. A post revision is saved for every change.
  • New: “Not broken” action (per row and in bulk) for links you have checked by hand. The link leaves the report and is only flagged again if it starts failing differently.
  • New: Redirect targets are shown under the status in the report.
  • New: “Replace” now also works for custom links in navigation menus.
  • New: “Settings” and “Broken Links” shortcuts on the Plugins screen.
  • Change: The “Delete” action was removed. It only deleted the report entry — the link stayed in the post and came back on the next scan. Use “Unlink”, “Replace” or “Not broken” instead.
  • Change: “Mark as Ignored” was removed — “Not broken” covers the same need without losing track of the link. Links you had ignored are converted to “not broken” automatically: they stay hidden, and are reported again only if they start failing differently.
  • Improvement: The report is now a single list of links that need attention: broken links first, then warnings, then redirects. Working links are still tracked in the background but no longer fill the list, and links waiting to be checked are shown as a count next to the scan button. The dashboard widget shows the Broken and Redirect counts.
  • Improvement: The “Scan Posts Now” and “Check Links Now” buttons are replaced by a single “Scan for broken links” button that finds and checks links in one go, with a two-step progress bar, a note on how often links are checked automatically, and the time of the last scan.
  • Improvement: Bulk actions now show a notice with the number of links affected and return to the same filtered view (the old “Link deleted” notice could appear twice).
  • Improvement: Each cron run now keeps processing batches for about 20 seconds instead of handling a single batch, so full scans and checks of large sites finish in a few runs instead of weeks.
  • Improvement: Email digest restyled to match the Beplus brand.
  • Fix: The scheduled scan never scanned navigation menus or widgets — only the manual scan button did.
  • Fix: Saving a post could delete the links of a navigation menu that happened to share the post’s ID.
  • Fix: Links from trashed, unpublished or deleted posts, and from deleted menus or widgets, stayed in the report and in email digests. Existing leftovers are cleaned up automatically on update.
  • Fix: Links removed from a post’s content stayed in the report until the link record was deleted by hand. Re-scanning now keeps the status of links that are still present and removes the ones that aren’t, instead of resetting every link to “Unchecked” on each save.
  • Fix: The email digest re-sent links that were already broken before the last email, and showed wrong titles for menu and widget links. It now lists only newly broken links, grouped by the post, menu or widget they were found in.
  • Fix: Re-checking or replacing a link from the report overwrote the “Type” badge instead of the “Status” badge until the page was reloaded.
  • Fix: Replacing a URL could strip backslashes from the post content.
  • Developer: New filters blss_request_args, blss_scannable_post_types and blss_cron_time_budget.

1.2.5

  • Fix: Redirects (301, 302, 303, 307, 308) were never actually detected — the link checker followed them internally before recording a result, so a moved link was reported as “OK” instead of “Redirect” and the redirect target was never saved. Redirects are now captured correctly, with the target URL stored for the report table.
  • Improvement: A redirect is now also followed (up to 5 hops) to confirm it actually leads to a live page — a link that redirects into a loop or to another broken URL is now reported as broken instead of a working redirect.

1.2.4

  • Improvement: Confirmed compatibility with WordPress 7.1.
  • Fix: Hardened sanitization of the CSV export action parameter and clarified direct filesystem/SQL usage that is required for CSV streaming and prepared queries.

1.2.3

  • Fix: Bulk actions (re-check, ignore, delete) could silently fail on sites running WordPress in a language other than English due to a security-check mismatch.
  • Fix: The “Link deleted” confirmation message wasn’t showing up after deleting a link from the report table.
  • Fix: Exported CSV files are now protected against formula/CSV injection when opened in spreadsheet apps like Excel or Google Sheets.
  • Fix: Root-relative and relative links (e.g. /contact or ../about) found in your content are now checked instead of being silently skipped.
  • Improvement: Renamed the internal “scan frequency” setting to “check frequency” to more accurately reflect that it controls how often links are checked, not how often content is scanned. Existing settings are migrated automatically — no action needed.
  • Improvement: Hardened a few admin-side output and script details for better security and code quality.
  • Added an “External services” section to the readme documenting the plugin’s link-checking HTTP requests.

1.2.2

  • Readme update: updated the “About BePlus” section, removed a promotional FAQ entry.

1.2.1

  • Readme update: added an “About BePlus” section, shortened the short description.

1.2.0

  • New: Multi-source scanning — broken images (<img src>), Gutenberg block URLs (embed, button, image, file blocks), ACF custom fields, navigation menus, and widget areas are now scanned in addition to post content anchors.
  • New: Link type column — every link in the report table is tagged with a color-coded badge (Anchor, Image, Block, ACF, Menu, Widget).
  • New: Export CSV tab — export all tracked links to a CSV file, with filters by status and link type. File includes UTF-8 BOM for Excel compatibility.
  • Improvement: Scan and check operations now show a real-time progress bar.

1.1.0

  • New: Inline replace link — click “Replace” on any link row to swap the URL directly from the admin table without editing the post manually.
  • The replacement updates both the database record and the actual post content.
  • Status is automatically reset to “Unchecked” after replacement so the new URL gets verified on the next check.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Automatic post scanning on save and via WP-Cron.
  • Admin report with WP_List_Table, status filters, and bulk actions.
  • Settings page (frequency, timeout, links per run, excluded patterns, email notifications).
  • Dashboard widget.
  • Email digest notification for new broken links.
